requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.

hunches.claim: The target-framework guard disables the feature on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on those targets. Consequently, generated code on those supported targets remains coverage-instrumented, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated except where the attribute cannot be emitted. The README's claim that these targets lack the attribute is also incorrect.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator with NetStandard20 reference assemblies and parse options defining NETSTANDARD2_0. First assert that compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName("System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute") is non-null, proving the attribute is available; then inspect active attributes on every generated class and assert ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is present. This fails on head because all occurrences of `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` exclude it. Repeat with .NET Framework reference assemblies and NETFRAMEWORK defined.

hunches.claim: The copy operation in MessagePackSecurity no longer copies HashCollisionResistant. A copy of a security configuration can therefore silently retain the destination's previous collision-resistance setting instead of the source's, potentially dropping hash-collision protection; this is an unrelated behavioral and security regression in a coverage-only change.

receipt_plan.detail: Add or run a unit test that creates a source MessagePackSecurity with HashCollisionResistant = true, performs the copy operation containing this hunk on a destination with HashCollisionResistant = false, and asserts the destination value is true. Also test propagation in the opposite direction. The first case fails after the removed assignment.

hunches.claim: Generated code targeting .NET Framework or .NET Standard 2.0 still has no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute because every template disables it under NETFRAMEWORK or NETSTANDARD2_0. The attribute is available on both targets, so these guards leave supported targets outside the requirement that all generated code be decorated.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ResolverRetainsExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnFrameworksWhereItExists for NETFRAMEWORK and NETSTANDARD2_0. Generate a resolver with those preprocessor symbols and assert that the resolver symbol has ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute; on head the conditional compilation removes it in both cases.

hunches.claim: The MessagePackSecurity copy constructor no longer copies HashCollisionResistant. For example, copying MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData (or calling WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth on it) silently produces an instance with hash-collision protection disabled, weakening security when the copy is used for untrusted input.

receipt_plan.detail: Run CopyingUntrustedSecurityRetainsHashCollisionResistance: construct new MessagePackSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData) and assert that HashCollisionResistant remains true. It fails on head because the property now retains its default value.

hunches.claim: The MessagePackSecurity copy constructor no longer preserves HashCollisionResistant, so cloning an existing security instance silently changes its behavior. This is unrelated to generated-code coverage and can weaken collision protection for users that copy UntrustedData or another configured instance.

receipt_plan.detail: Add or run a unit test constructing MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, copying it with new MessagePackSecurity(original), and asserting copy.HashCollisionResistant == original.HashCollisionResistant; repeat with a security instance whose HashCollisionResistant value is explicitly configured. The head copy will retain its default instead.

hunches.claim: The MessagePackSecurity copy constructor no longer preserves HashCollisionResistant. Cloning MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData therefore produces an instance with the default false value, silently disabling collision-resistant hashing and re-exposing deserialized untrusted maps to hash-collision denial-of-service attacks.

receipt_plan.detail: Create a derived MessagePackSecurity instance by copying MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData (or clone it through WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth), then assert that the copy.HashCollisionResistant is true. Also deserialize a string-keyed map using the copied options under a deterministic collision scenario and verify that the collision-resistant comparer is still used.

hunches.claim: The unrelated MessagePackSecurity copy change silently drops HashCollisionResistant when security options are copied. A copy of options configured for collision-resistant hashing can therefore revert to the destination's existing/default value, weakening protection for untrusted data; this is contrary to the product's recorded collision-resistance behavior and is outside REQ-2297.

receipt_plan.detail: Add or run a MessagePackSecurity copy-constructor/CopyFrom test: configure the source with HashCollisionResistant = true, copy it into another instance, and assert the destination remains true. Also verify the remaining security properties are preserved. The changed line makes this assertion fail.

hunches.claim: The new tests check only that each generated file contains at least one guarded attribute, not that every generated type is decorated. Resolver and composite-resolver files contain several newly decorated types, so deleting the attribute from FormatterCache<T> or the formatter helper leaves both assertions passing: the file still contains another attribute, and guardedCount is recalculated from the reduced output.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs:55 delete-statement: 	[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] -> (deleted); expected to survive in CodeCoverageExclusionTests because the resolver class and GetFormatterHelper attributes remain, AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage uses only file-level Contains, and ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable compares occurrence counts within that same mutated output

hunches.claim: No test in the change covers MessagePackSecurity's copy constructor, so removal of the HashCollisionResistant assignment is unprotected. A regression test copying an instance with this property set and asserting the copied value would have failed on this change.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs:63 delete-statement: this.HashCollisionResistant = copyFrom.HashCollisionResistant; -> (deleted, immediately before MaximumObjectGraphDepth assignment); expected to survive because the diff adds only source-generation attribute tests and no security copy-constructor test

refused.what: Which reading of REQ-2297 is intended (A or B)

residual_risk: This change touches 238 files (222 generated) in codegen-templates, security, tests; the highest routed risk is 8/10. 15 file(s) were routed for deep review, 1 for light review and 222 to the regeneration check. The existing source generator tests ran on head: 169 of 169 passed, 0 failed. 9 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. It touches risky areas (codegen-templates, security), so a human must sign off. 5 thing(s) were not checked, including mutation testing; generated formatter bytes (source generator output, base vs head); A/B review branches. By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The AI did not choose between the readings; whoever merges A or B owns that product decision and the receipts of the branch they merge.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated type—including formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, and resolvers—with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally and provide no setting. Code: Update all relevant source-generator transforms so every emitted generated type receives the attribute, conditionally emitting it only as needed for target-framework compatibility, and update all affected verified snapshots; unlike the narrower reading, resolver and other non-formatter generated types are included, and unlike the opt-out reading no configuration API is added.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Apply ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally only to generated formatter types, leaving non-formatter generated code such as resolvers without the attribute. Code: Change the formatter-related transforms and their snapshots but not resolver or other generated-type templates; the emitted coverage behavior and scope of modified snapshots differ from the all-generated-types reading.
